title: incident-bot: refactor on-call autodiagnostics pipeline and compact runbook storage
author: Aisha Ramos
description: Motivation: the on-call autodiagnostics pipeline has grown organic complexity over multiple feature PRs. This causes slow rule evaluation, high memory use during runbook generation, and duplicated runbook fragments across SLO-toolkit outputs. This PR refactors the autodiagnostics orchestration into a single pipeline with clear stages (signal collection -> prioritization -> runbook synthesis), compacts runbook storage using a canonical fragment store, and adds deterministic unit tests and benchmarks. Changes include: canonical runbook fragment cache, stateless pipeline stages, backpressure-aware queueing, and compact on-disk storage for precomputed runbook snippets. Checklist: - [x] refactor pipeline into stages - [x] implement fragment store with dedup keys - [x] add unit + integration tests - [x] add microbenchmarks for evaluation latency - [x] update runbook templates and docs - [x] migration script for existing cached fragments Backwards compatibility: pipeline preserves existing public incident-bot CLI flags and webhooks. A small migration step (one-time) consolidates previously duplicated runbook fragments into the new fragment store. Rollout plan: feature branch tested in staging, deploy behind a feature flag, run migration job during off-peak, toggle feature flag after 48h of stability monitoring. Related work: references ENG-3456 (autodiagnostics reliability), SRE-778 (runbook consolidation), earlier PRs pr-189432 and pr-170543.
